# Agentic Engineering Org

Build a reusable **template repository** that encodes a one-person AI software
enterprise: tool-locked role subagents do triage, spec, test authoring,
implementation, and review, while a single human ("the founder") holds
architecture and merge authority. Two deterministic hook gates make the boundary
real — **agents never merge**, and **no one commits a red suite**. A vendored
behavior-first TDD harness and a GitHub-native sprint workflow tie it together.

You are building the *template* (working name `ai-enterprise-template`), not a
specific product. The founder reuses it to start future products.

## Operating rules (read before doing anything)

1. **Work phase by phase, in order.** Finish a phase, run its verification, then
   stop at its checkpoint. Do not skip, reorder, or batch phases.
2. **This is a supervised build.** At every **⛔ CHECKPOINT**, stop and wait for an
   explicit "approved" from the founder. Do not infer approval.
3. **You never do these; you prepare them and ask the founder to run/approve them:**
   merging to `main`, enabling or changing branch protection, deleting any branch or
   data, pushing to `main`. These are the gates this enterprise is built around.
4. **Do all work on a branch** named `setup/<phase-slug>` (e.g. `setup/00-foundation`).
   The founder reviews and merges. You are dogfooding the workflow you build.
5. **Report after each phase** with exactly one status —
   `DONE` / `DONE_WITH_CONCERNS` / `BLOCKED` / `NEEDS_CONTEXT` — then say what you
   produced and what the founder should check.
6. **Verify mechanics against current docs before writing them.** Subagent
   frontmatter, hook schema, and slash-command behavior drift. The skeletons in the
   `references/` files are a starting point *already corrected against the docs as of
   this skill's authoring*, but re-check the URLs in "Reference material" and note any
   divergence in the Decision Log.
7. **If a spec is ambiguous, contradictory, or wrong, stop and raise it**
   (`NEEDS_CONTEXT`). Do not guess and do not silently "fix" it.
8. **Keep the test baseline green.** Once the tests-green hook exists (Phase 3), a red
   suite blocks your own commits. That is intended — you live under your own gates.

## Locked decisions (hard constraints — do not relitigate)

| # | Constraint |
|---|------------|
| DEC-1 | Test authorship is split. The **outer acceptance test is the behavioral contract** — authored by the spec/test-author role, committed red, then locked. The **implementer drives inner unit cycles only** and may not edit the outer test or the specs. |
| DEC-2 | Roles are **addressable subagent files** in `.claude/agents/`, each with a locked `tools` set and a pinned `model`. |
| DEC-3 | Two gates are **deterministic hooks**, not advice: *agents-never-merge* and *tests-green-before-commit*. Branch protection backstops them server-side. |
| DEC-4 | **GitHub issues and PRs** are the system of record. Sprints, not sessions. |
| DEC-5 | One repository. Spec and build are separated by **role and a spec-freeze hook**, not by folder. |
| DEC-6 | The behavior-first loop is the **vendored `brainqub3/red-green-refactor` harness** (MIT), adapted to the roles and gates — not hand-built. |
| DEC-7 | DEC-4 runs through the **installed GitHub plugin** (issue/PR tools), not raw `gh` in Bash. Consequence: the *agents-never-merge* gate must also match the plugin's merge-capable tool, not only `Bash(git merge …)`. |

## Role roster (the contract for Phases 2–3)

The founder is the main session and is **not** a subagent.

| Role | `tools` (capability) | `model` | Path rule (enforced by hooks, not `tools`) |
|------|----------------------|---------|--------------------------------------------|
| Triage / PM  | Read, Grep, Glob, Bash              | haiku  | Writes no code |
| Spec author  | Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write       | opus   | May write only under `specs/` |
| Test author  | Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash | sonnet | May write only under `tests/` |
| Implementer  | Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash | sonnet (escalate to opus on complex slices) | May **not** write under `tests/` or `specs/` |
| Reviewer     | Read, Grep, Glob, Bash              | sonnet | Writes nothing (read-only, achieved by withholding Edit/Write) |

> **Why hooks, not `tools`, for path rules.** The `tools` field grants or withholds
> whole tool *types*; it cannot scope a tool to a path. "Spec author writes only
> `specs/`" etc. are enforced by **PreToolUse hooks declared in each subagent's own
> frontmatter**, so the rule is scoped to that role. The reviewer is the exception:
> read-only comes purely from withholding Edit and Write.

## Corrections already applied (verified against current docs)

The source brief predates some schema changes. The `references/` skeletons already
reflect these; keep them in mind if you regenerate anything:

- **`/agents` is no longer an interactive wizard.** Write/edit `.claude/agents/*.md`

  directory, which needs one restart.
- **Hooks read tool input from stdin as JSON, not from env vars.** There is no

- **The `if:` field on hook objects is real** (permission-rule syntax, e.g.
  `"Bash(git merge *)"`, `"Edit(specs/**)"`). Per-subagent frontmatter `hooks:` are
  also real. Both are used deliberately here.
- **The installed GitHub plugin's tool namespace is `mcp__plugin_github_github__…`**
  (e.g. `mcp__plugin_github_github__merge_pull_request`). Confirm the exact names in
  Phase 0 with `/plugin`; the merge gate must match whatever they actually are.

- Subagents & `/agents`: `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents`
- Hooks (events, `if` matcher, exit-code 2, MCP tool matching): `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks`
- Plugins (what the GitHub plugin bundles; `pr-review-toolkit`): `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins`

## Toolchain & stack profile (verify in Phase 0)

Assumed present, stop (`BLOCKED`) if missing: `git`, `gh` (authenticated), a recent
Claude Code with the **official GitHub plugin/connector** installed, and **Node 18+**
(the harness needs it). The stack is **profile-driven**: the **default profile is
Python 3.13+ with `uv`, `pytest`, `ruff`**. Wherever a concrete command appears (e.g.
`uv run pytest` in a hook), read it as "the profile's test/lint command" and swap in
the project's real toolchain. Detect the stack in Phase 0 and record the profile in
the Decision Log.

## The build — phase by phase

Each phase is **Goal → do the work (see reference) → Verify → Checkpoint.** Full
skeletons live in `references/`; load the named file when you reach the phase.

### Phase 0 — Repository foundation
**Goal:** an empty but valid template repo with a green baseline and a remote.
- Verify the toolchain above. Run `/plugin` and **record exactly what the GitHub
  plugin bundles — its commands, agents, and especially its MCP tool names, including
  the merge-PR tool.** Phases 3 and 5 depend on these names.
- Create the directory tree in `references/directory-tree.md`. Add a trivial passing
  test so the suite is green from commit one. Init `git`, commit on `main`.
- **Prepare (do not run)** the `gh repo create` command and the branch-protection
  command (require PR before merge, require status checks, block direct push to
  `main`). Present both for the founder to run.

**Verify:** dependency install succeeds; the suite runs green (default: `uv sync`
then `uv run pytest`); `git log` shows one commit.
**⛔ CHECKPOINT 0:** founder runs `gh repo create` and enables branch protection. Do
not proceed until confirmed.

### Phase 1 — `CLAUDE.md` handbook (the constitution)
**Goal:** a short, project-agnostic handbook every session and subagent inherits.
Write it per `references/claude-md-handbook.md` (the four-level hierarchy, role
boundaries and who may merge, spec-freeze & drift-to-issue rules, the behavior-first
loop and DEC-1, the two gates, model-tiering guidance, prose conventions). Keep it
under ~200 lines.

**Verify:** a fresh reader of `CLAUDE.md` *alone* can answer "who may merge?" and "who
may edit specs, and when?".
**⛔ CHECKPOINT 1:** founder approves the handbook wording.

### Phase 2 — Role subagents
**Goal:** the five roles as addressable, tool-locked, model-pinned subagents.
Write `.claude/agents/{triage,spec-author,test-author,implementer,reviewer}.md`
directly (the `/agents` command no longer authors them; files hot-reload). Use the
frontmatter + path-guard + system-prompt skeletons in `references/agents.md`. Apply
the roster exactly: reviewer gets **no** Edit/Write; spec-author, test-author, and
implementer carry frontmatter `PreToolUse` path guards (allow their own area, deny
others). Give the reviewer a **two-stage review** (spec-compliance first, then
code-quality); before writing it from scratch, inspect the official
`pr-review-toolkit` plugin and reuse it **only if** the two-stage ordering and the
"does the test encode intent?" check are preserved.

**Verify:** all five load live (check them listed / delegable); reviewer has no write
capability. (Path guards are proven in Phase 3, once `deny.sh` exists.)
**⛔ CHECKPOINT 2:** founder reviews each role's tools, model, prompt, and the
`pr-review-toolkit` reuse decision.

### Phase 3 — Hard gates (hooks) — the most important phase
**Goal:** the two deterministic gates plus the path-guard helper, all enforced by
exit code 2. Build every script and the `settings.json` wiring from
`references/hooks.md`. In summary:
- `deny.sh` — prints a reason to stderr, `exit 2`. Backs the role path guards.
- `block-merge.sh` — `exit 2` with a reason. Wired as a `Bash` `PreToolUse` hook
  gated by `if` on `git merge *` and `git push * main*`, and blocks direct commits on
  `main`. **Also add an MCP matcher** for the GitHub plugin's merge-capable tool
  (from Phase 0, e.g. `mcp__plugin_github_github__merge_pull_request`) → the Bash
  rules can't see a plugin-driven merge (DEC-7).
- `tests-green.sh` — runs the profile's test command; `exit 2` if red. Wired as a
  `Bash` `PreToolUse` hook gated by `if: Bash(git commit *)`. Keep it fast.
- **Spec-freeze hook** — `PreToolUse` on `Edit|Write` gated by `if: Edit(specs/**)`,
  blocking spec edits during implementation. The spec-author works with this global
  hook disabled (it relies on its own frontmatter allow instead); document how the
  founder toggles spec-authoring mode.
- Make all hook scripts executable.

**Verify (live, show transcripts):** a `git merge` from a session is blocked with a
reason; a merge through the **GitHub plugin's merge tool** is blocked; a `git commit`
with a deliberately failing test is blocked, then reverting to green allows it; the
implementer subagent attempting to edit under `tests/` is blocked; `/hooks` lists all
configured hooks.
**⛔ CHECKPOINT 3:** founder confirms **each** gate fires, including the plugin merge
path. Do not proceed on an unverified gate.

### Phase 4 — Vendor & adapt the TDD harness (DEC-6)
**Goal:** the `brainqub3/red-green-refactor` suite living in `.claude/skills/`,
adapted to the roles, gates, and Python/non-web stack. Follow
`references/harness-and-sprint.md` (§ Harness). Key points: vendor by copy (record
the source commit SHA); **audit the scripts before trusting them**; adapt
`red-green-refactor` so the outer acceptance test is authored/locked by the
spec/test-author and the implementer drives inner cycles only; adapt `tdd-plan` to
write per-slice plans under `plans/<feature>/` linked to a GitHub issue; adapt
`tdd-ci` to run the profile's test command and commit an Actions workflow (never
commit secrets); adapt `safe-pr` to the **non-web evidence path** (real-endpoint
integration + transcript evidence), Playwright optional.

**Verify:** `/tdd-plan` writes slice plans; `/red-green-refactor` drives one slice
red→green with the outer test locked against the implementer; `/tdd-ci` yields a
passing Actions run; `/safe-pr` prepares a PR into `main` with embedded evidence and
**does not merge**.
**⛔ CHECKPOINT 4:** founder confirms the audit findings and the DEC-1 adaptation.

### Phase 5 — Sprint & role wiring over the harness
**Goal:** thin management skills that replace the session model and drive the roles
through the harness. Follow `references/harness-and-sprint.md` (§ Sprint). Write
`/sprint-plan` (decompose a subproject into a GitHub-issue backlog **through the
plugin's issue tools**, each issue linking its `plans/<feature>/` slice files; draft
issue bodies to local files for operator review before filing); `/sprint-start`
(clear context, pick the next issue by dependency, drive the roles through the
harness — outer test red → implementer greens inner cycles → reviewer two-stage →
`safe-pr` prepares the PR, never merges); thin `/triage` and `/review` entry points;
and define GitHub labels `spec-drift`, `blocked`, `needs-context`,
`done-with-concerns` plus a per-subproject namespace convention.

**Verify:** `/sprint-plan` on a sample PRD produces real issues with linked slice
plans; `/sprint-start` drives one issue from selection to a prepared PR with no manual
git, and **no implementation commit precedes its slice's red outer test**.
**⛔ CHECKPOINT 5:** founder approves the sprint flow on the sample.

### Phase 6 — Dry run & validation
**Goal:** prove the whole machine on one throwaway feature, in a **fresh session** so
all subagents and hooks are active. Take one trivial feature end to end: idea →
`/triage` issue → spec-author contract + test-author red outer test → implementer
green → reviewer two-stage → `/safe-pr` PR into `main`. **Stop at the merge.** Present
the green, reviewed PR to the founder.

**Verify:** every item in the Definition of Done below holds on the dry run.
**⛔ CHECKPOINT 6:** the founder performs the merge. **You must not.** After merge,
optionally demonstrate `/safe-cleanup` in dry-run (report-only).

> *Migration note (only if adopting this into a project that already had a different
> workflow): archive any prior session-based planning/execution skills to `archive/`,

> split across dirs → one repo with role separation + spec-freeze hook), and remove
> stale assumptions (hard-coded multi-workspace paths). Skip entirely if starting

---

## Decision Log & Progress Tracker

Maintain both as you work. Append a **Decision Log** row whenever you diverge from a
skeleton (e.g. a hook field renamed per current docs) or resolve an ambiguity — seed
it with DEC-1..7 and the chosen stack profile. Keep a **Progress Tracker** with one
row per phase (Status / Date / Notes). Store them in `docs/` or the repo README so the
founder can audit the build.

## Definition of done

- [ ] A new product starts from the template: PRD in `specs/`, `/sprint-plan` yields a
      real issue backlog with linked slice plans.
- [ ] Five roles exist as tool-locked, model-pinned subagents; reviewer is read-only;
      implementer is hook-blocked from `tests/` and `specs/`.
- [ ] `git merge`, pushes to `main`, **and the GitHub plugin's merge tool** are all
      blocked from any agent by a hook; branch protection backstops it.
- [ ] A failing suite blocks a commit; the spec area is frozen during implementation.
- [ ] Harness vendored and adapted: outer acceptance test is the locked contract;

- [ ] No implementation commit precedes its slice's red outer test.
- [ ] Spec drift routes to a `spec-drift` issue, never an in-place patch.
- [ ] The operator acts at exactly three moments: plan approval, drift adjudication,

When all hold: the operator specifies and decides, the roles build and check, the
gates hold the line.

# Agentic Engineering Org

Build a reusable **template repository** that encodes a one-person AI software
enterprise: tool-locked role subagents do triage, spec, test authoring,
implementation, and review, while a single human ("the founder") holds
architecture and merge authority. Two deterministic hook gates make the boundary
real — **agents never merge**, and **no one commits a red suite**. A vendored
behavior-first TDD harness and a GitHub-native sprint workflow tie it together.

You are building the *template* (working name `ai-enterprise-template`), not a
specific product. The founder reuses it to start future products.

## Operating rules (read before doing anything)

1. **Work phase by phase, in order.** Finish a phase, run its verification, then
   stop at its checkpoint. Do not skip, reorder, or batch phases.
2. **This is a supervised build.** At every **⛔ CHECKPOINT**, stop and wait for an
   explicit "approved" from the founder. Do not infer approval.
3. **You never do these; you prepare them and ask the founder to run/approve them:**
   merging to `main`, enabling or changing branch protection, deleting any branch or
   data, pushing to `main`. These are the gates this enterprise is built around.
4. **Do all work on a branch** named `setup/<phase-slug>` (e.g. `setup/00-foundation`).
   The founder reviews and merges. You are dogfooding the workflow you build.
5. **Report after each phase** with exactly one status —
   `DONE` / `DONE_WITH_CONCERNS` / `BLOCKED` / `NEEDS_CONTEXT` — then say what you
   produced and what the founder should check.
6. **Verify mechanics against current docs before writing them.** Subagent
   frontmatter, hook schema, and slash-command behavior drift. The skeletons in the
   `references/` files are a starting point *already corrected against the docs as of
   this skill's authoring*, but re-check the URLs in "Reference material" and note any
   divergence in the Decision Log.
7. **If a spec is ambiguous, contradictory, or wrong, stop and raise it**
   (`NEEDS_CONTEXT`). Do not guess and do not silently "fix" it.
8. **Keep the test baseline green.** Once the tests-green hook exists (Phase 3), a red
   suite blocks your own commits. That is intended — you live under your own gates.

## Locked decisions (hard constraints — do not relitigate)

| # | Constraint |
|---|------------|
| DEC-1 | Test authorship is split. The **outer acceptance test is the behavioral contract** — authored by the spec/test-author role, committed red, then locked. The **implementer drives inner unit cycles only** and may not edit the outer test or the specs. |
| DEC-2 | Roles are **addressable subagent files** in `.claude/agents/`, each with a locked `tools` set and a pinned `model`. |
| DEC-3 | Two gates are **deterministic hooks**, not advice: *agents-never-merge* and *tests-green-before-commit*. Branch protection backstops them server-side. |
| DEC-4 | **GitHub issues and PRs** are the system of record. Sprints, not sessions. |
| DEC-5 | One repository. Spec and build are separated by **role and a spec-freeze hook**, not by folder. |
| DEC-6 | The behavior-first loop is the **vendored `brainqub3/red-green-refactor` harness** (MIT), adapted to the roles and gates — not hand-built. |
| DEC-7 | DEC-4 runs through the **installed GitHub plugin** (issue/PR tools), not raw `gh` in Bash. Consequence: the *agents-never-merge* gate must also match the plugin's merge-capable tool, not only `Bash(git merge …)`. |

## Role roster (the contract for Phases 2–3)

The founder is the main session and is **not** a subagent.

| Role | `tools` (capability) | `model` | Path rule (enforced by hooks, not `tools`) |
|------|----------------------|---------|--------------------------------------------|
| Triage / PM  | Read, Grep, Glob, Bash              | haiku  | Writes no code |
| Spec author  | Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write       | opus   | May write only under `specs/` |
| Test author  | Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash | sonnet | May write only under `tests/` |
| Implementer  | Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash | sonnet (escalate to opus on complex slices) | May **not** write under `tests/` or `specs/` |
| Reviewer     | Read, Grep, Glob, Bash              | sonnet | Writes nothing (read-only, achieved by withholding Edit/Write) |

> **Why hooks, not `tools`, for path rules.** The `tools` field grants or withholds
> whole tool *types*; it cannot scope a tool to a path. "Spec author writes only
> `specs/`" etc. are enforced by **PreToolUse hooks declared in each subagent's own
> frontmatter**, so the rule is scoped to that role. The reviewer is the exception:
> read-only comes purely from withholding Edit and Write.

## The build — phase by phase

Each phase is **Goal → do the work (see reference) → Verify → Checkpoint.** Full
skeletons live in `references/`; load the named file when you reach the phase.

### Phase 0 — Repository foundation
**Goal:** an empty but valid template repo with a green baseline and a remote.
- Verify the toolchain above. Run `/plugin` and **record exactly what the GitHub
  plugin bundles — its commands, agents, and especially its MCP tool names, including
  the merge-PR tool.** Phases 3 and 5 depend on these names.
- Create the directory tree in `references/directory-tree.md`. Add a trivial passing
  test so the suite is green from commit one. Init `git`, commit on `main`.
- **Prepare (do not run)** the `gh repo create` command and the branch-protection
  command (require PR before merge, require status checks, block direct push to
  `main`). Present both for the founder to run.

**Verify:** dependency install succeeds; the suite runs green (default: `uv sync`
then `uv run pytest`); `git log` shows one commit.
**⛔ CHECKPOINT 0:** founder runs `gh repo create` and enables branch protection. Do
not proceed until confirmed.

### Phase 1 — `CLAUDE.md` handbook (the constitution)
**Goal:** a short, project-agnostic handbook every session and subagent inherits.
Write it per `references/claude-md-handbook.md` (the four-level hierarchy, role
boundaries and who may merge, spec-freeze & drift-to-issue rules, the behavior-first
loop and DEC-1, the two gates, model-tiering guidance, prose conventions). Keep it
under ~200 lines.

**Verify:** a fresh reader of `CLAUDE.md` *alone* can answer "who may merge?" and "who
may edit specs, and when?".
**⛔ CHECKPOINT 1:** founder approves the handbook wording.

### Phase 2 — Role subagents
**Goal:** the five roles as addressable, tool-locked, model-pinned subagents.
Write `.claude/agents/{triage,spec-author,test-author,implementer,reviewer}.md`
directly (the `/agents` command no longer authors them; files hot-reload). Use the
frontmatter + path-guard + system-prompt skeletons in `references/agents.md`. Apply
the roster exactly: reviewer gets **no** Edit/Write; spec-author, test-author, and
implementer carry frontmatter `PreToolUse` path guards (allow their own area, deny
others). Give the reviewer a **two-stage review** (spec-compliance first, then
code-quality); before writing it from scratch, inspect the official
`pr-review-toolkit` plugin and reuse it **only if** the two-stage ordering and the
"does the test encode intent?" check are preserved.

**Verify:** all five load live (check them listed / delegable); reviewer has no write
capability. (Path guards are proven in Phase 3, once `deny.sh` exists.)
**⛔ CHECKPOINT 2:** founder reviews each role's tools, model, prompt, and the
`pr-review-toolkit` reuse decision.

### Phase 3 — Hard gates (hooks) — the most important phase
**Goal:** the two deterministic gates plus the path-guard helper, all enforced by
exit code 2. Build every script and the `settings.json` wiring from
`references/hooks.md`. In summary:
- `deny.sh` — prints a reason to stderr, `exit 2`. Backs the role path guards.
- `block-merge.sh` — `exit 2` with a reason. Wired as a `Bash` `PreToolUse` hook
  gated by `if` on `git merge *` and `git push * main*`, and blocks direct commits on
  `main`. **Also add an MCP matcher** for the GitHub plugin's merge-capable tool
  (from Phase 0, e.g. `mcp__plugin_github_github__merge_pull_request`) → the Bash
  rules can't see a plugin-driven merge (DEC-7).
- `tests-green.sh` — runs the profile's test command; `exit 2` if red. Wired as a
  `Bash` `PreToolUse` hook gated by `if: Bash(git commit *)`. Keep it fast.
- **Spec-freeze hook** — `PreToolUse` on `Edit|Write` gated by `if: Edit(specs/**)`,
  blocking spec edits during implementation. The spec-author works with this global
  hook disabled (it relies on its own frontmatter allow instead); document how the
  founder toggles spec-authoring mode.
- Make all hook scripts executable.

**Verify (live, show transcripts):** a `git merge` from a session is blocked with a
reason; a merge through the **GitHub plugin's merge tool** is blocked; a `git commit`
with a deliberately failing test is blocked, then reverting to green allows it; the
implementer subagent attempting to edit under `tests/` is blocked; `/hooks` lists all
configured hooks.
**⛔ CHECKPOINT 3:** founder confirms **each** gate fires, including the plugin merge
path. Do not proceed on an unverified gate.

### Phase 4 — Vendor & adapt the TDD harness (DEC-6)
**Goal:** the `brainqub3/red-green-refactor` suite living in `.claude/skills/`,
adapted to the roles, gates, and Python/non-web stack. Follow
`references/harness-and-sprint.md` (§ Harness). Key points: vendor by copy (record
the source commit SHA); **audit the scripts before trusting them**; adapt
`red-green-refactor` so the outer acceptance test is authored/locked by the
spec/test-author and the implementer drives inner cycles only; adapt `tdd-plan` to
write per-slice plans under `plans/<feature>/` linked to a GitHub issue; adapt
`tdd-ci` to run the profile's test command and commit an Actions workflow (never
commit secrets); adapt `safe-pr` to the **non-web evidence path** (real-endpoint
integration + transcript evidence), Playwright optional.

**Verify:** `/tdd-plan` writes slice plans; `/red-green-refactor` drives one slice
red→green with the outer test locked against the implementer; `/tdd-ci` yields a
passing Actions run; `/safe-pr` prepares a PR into `main` with embedded evidence and
**does not merge**.
**⛔ CHECKPOINT 4:** founder confirms the audit findings and the DEC-1 adaptation.

### Phase 5 — Sprint & role wiring over the harness
**Goal:** thin management skills that replace the session model and drive the roles
through the harness. Follow `references/harness-and-sprint.md` (§ Sprint). Write
`/sprint-plan` (decompose a subproject into a GitHub-issue backlog **through the
plugin's issue tools**, each issue linking its `plans/<feature>/` slice files; draft
issue bodies to local files for operator review before filing); `/sprint-start`
(clear context, pick the next issue by dependency, drive the roles through the
harness — outer test red → implementer greens inner cycles → reviewer two-stage →
`safe-pr` prepares the PR, never merges); thin `/triage` and `/review` entry points;
and define GitHub labels `spec-drift`, `blocked`, `needs-context`,
`done-with-concerns` plus a per-subproject namespace convention.

**Verify:** `/sprint-plan` on a sample PRD produces real issues with linked slice
plans; `/sprint-start` drives one issue from selection to a prepared PR with no manual
git, and **no implementation commit precedes its slice's red outer test**.
**⛔ CHECKPOINT 5:** founder approves the sprint flow on the sample.

### Phase 6 — Dry run & validation
**Goal:** prove the whole machine on one throwaway feature, in a **fresh session** so
all subagents and hooks are active. Take one trivial feature end to end: idea →
`/triage` issue → spec-author contract + test-author red outer test → implementer
green → reviewer two-stage → `/safe-pr` PR into `main`. **Stop at the merge.** Present
the green, reviewed PR to the founder.

**Verify:** every item in the Definition of Done below holds on the dry run.
**⛔ CHECKPOINT 6:** the founder performs the merge. **You must not.** After merge,
optionally demonstrate `/safe-cleanup` in dry-run (report-only).

> *Migration note (only if adopting this into a project that already had a different
> workflow): archive any prior session-based planning/execution skills to `archive/`,
> write a short `MIGRATION.md` mapping old constructs (session/handoff notes →
> issue/PR threads; standalone decision log → issues or `DECISIONS.md`; spec/code
> split across dirs → one repo with role separation + spec-freeze hook), and remove
> stale assumptions (hard-coded multi-workspace paths). Skip entirely if starting
> fresh.*

## Decision Log & Progress Tracker

Maintain both as you work. Append a **Decision Log** row whenever you diverge from a
skeleton (e.g. a hook field renamed per current docs) or resolve an ambiguity — seed
it with DEC-1..7 and the chosen stack profile. Keep a **Progress Tracker** with one

founder can audit the build.

## Definition of done

- [ ] A new product starts from the template: PRD in `specs/`, `/sprint-plan` yields a
      real issue backlog with linked slice plans.
- [ ] Five roles exist as tool-locked, model-pinned subagents; reviewer is read-only;
      implementer is hook-blocked from `tests/` and `specs/`.
- [ ] `git merge`, pushes to `main`, **and the GitHub plugin's merge tool** are all
      blocked from any agent by a hook; branch protection backstops it.
- [ ] A failing suite blocks a commit; the spec area is frozen during implementation.
- [ ] Harness vendored and adapted: outer acceptance test is the locked contract;
      `tdd-ci` runs the profile's test command in Actions; `safe-pr` uses the non-web
      evidence path.
- [ ] No implementation commit precedes its slice's red outer test.
- [ ] Spec drift routes to a `spec-drift` issue, never an in-place patch.
- [ ] The operator acts at exactly three moments: plan approval, drift adjudication,
      merge — and every checkpoint was approved before proceeding.

When all hold: the operator specifies and decides, the roles build and check, the
gates hold the line.
